claims.text: The repository source explicitly identifies LeetCode 59 Spiral Matrix II; under that mapping the task is to generate an n x n matrix with 1..n^2 in spiral order.
The exact boundary-shrinking Java implementation matches a structurally different direction+visited oracle for all n=1..20 and produces each value 1..n^2 exactly once.
Implementation language, required algorithm and behavior outside the positive-n problem domain are not preserved source constraints; the candidate labels these as answer-side choices.

findings: The repository source explicitly identifies LeetCode 59 Spiral Matrix II, so the problem identity is recoverable without guessing.
The candidate separates source-preserved problem identity from answer-side implementation language, boundary-shrinking algorithm and defensive invalid-input behavior.
The four-boundary loop states a clear unfilled-rectangle invariant and guards the final single-row/single-column layer before writing the bottom and left edges.
The exact Java implementation matches a structurally different direction-plus-visited oracle for every n from 1 through 20 and preserves the 1..n^2 permutation invariant.
The candidate correctly reports O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary state excluding the required output matrix, and distinguishes Spiral Matrix II generation from Spiral Matrix I traversal.
No project experience, production metric, source constraint or implementation requirement is fabricated.
Formal promotion remains governed by repository promotion, required human approval and real-review policy.
